name: Secundus
overview: Secundus is a male believer identified in the New Testament as being from Thessalonica. Beyond this designation, Scripture does not provide additional personal or tribal details about him. His mention highlights his role as a member of the early Christian community in that city.
namesAndTitles: The name Secundus appears only once in Scripture and carries no recorded meaning or divine origin. It is presented simply as a proper name without additional significance provided in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Secundus beyond his identification as a believer from Thessalonica. There are no listed connections to other individuals in the biblical narrative.
scriptureSignificance: Secundus is noted in Acts 20:4 as one of the believers accompanying Paul, indicating his involvement in the missionary efforts of the early church. His inclusion demonstrates the participation of Thessalonian Christians in the spread of the gospel and the support network surrounding the apostle Paul. Though briefly mentioned, Secundus represents the faithful who contributed to the advancement of Christ's kingdom during the formative years of the church.
